page.layout: One page of running text in one column, full width. Running head at top right, page number at top left. No marginal notes. A Latin verse quotation (Persius and Juvenal) is set in italic, indented, within the text. The page ends with a short right-aligned last line.

main_text.p: & ritu hoc toto confule Harpocrationem. Atque hæc sacra cum peregissent, non ante domum redibant quàm & vestem & corpus aqua vel fluuiali, vel fontana purificassent. Porphyrius, Πάντες ἐν τέ-τῳ ὠμολόγῳ(ν) οἱ Θεολόγοι, ὡς ἄντε ἄτοκον ἐν ταῖς ἀπορροπαιοις θυσίαις τῇ θυομένῳ, καὶ καθαροῖς τε χρηστέον, μὴ γὰρ ἵνα τὶς εἰς ἄσυ, μηδ᾽ εἰς οἶκον ἴδιον, μὴ πρότερον ἐδήσῃ ἡ σώματ ποδαμοῖς ἡ πηγὴ ἀποκαθάρας. ἡ κεφαλῆς λούσθω. ) Colligi hinc posse videtur in triuiis fuisse ἀφραντίσια. potest tamen etiam aliter accipi. Ritum lauandi capitis in purificationibus exprimit Persius,

p.i: — Tiberino in gurgite mergis Mane caput bis, terque. & Iuuenalis Ter matutino Tiberi mergetur, & ipsis Vorticibus timidum caput abluet.

main_text.p: σχίλλῃ ἢ σχύλακι κελάσαι αὐτὸν ἀφικαθάραι.) Tangit duplicem veterum confuetudinem expiandi lustrandiqué se. altera erat, circumaćta circa corpus scilla: altera catulo similiter circa corpus du-ćto. Hoc enim significat ἀφικαθάραι. De scilla, quòd expiandi vim crederetur habere, notum vel ex Plinio & medicorum libris. Artemidorus Ἐνοδίῳ. Ἡ σκίλλα καθάρσιον ἐν νεκρομάντει. Lucianus Ἐπισκοπεῖ τις. ἐκάθηρέ τί με, ἢ ἀπέμαξε, ἢ ἀφηγνίζει δαδὶ καὶ σκίλλῃ ἢ ἄλλοις πλέοσι. Dio Chrysostomus oratione XLVIII. ἀλλά μοι δοκεῖ ἀφικαθάρσεως τῷ ἀστρὶ μὴ σκίλλῃ μηδὲ ὑδάλις, ἀλλὰ πολὺ καθαρωτέρῳ χρήματι λόγῳ κοινῷ πράξειν. Plura Clemens Alexand. septimo Stromat. & Theocriti scholiastes in Thalysiis. De catulo, res minus vulgò, vt videtur, nota: quare etiam eius ritus ignoratione interpretes miris modis hunc

page.notes: The Greek text is only partly legible on the scan. Several Greek words and accents were read with uncertainty and are not marked individually here; the Greek lines in the Porphyrius and Dio Chrysostomus quotations, and the Ἐνοδίῳ and ἀφικαθάραι forms, should be checked against a clearer image. Latin words are transcribed as printed (long s is plain s; u/v and i/j normalised). The last line "dis hunc" is set at the right and is the continuation of the hyphenated word "mo-" and so is treated as text, not as a catchword. The Persius and Juvenal verse is treated as a single verse paragraph in italics. The attribution "& Iuuenalis" stands on the first verse line. The Greek word "ἀφραντίσια" and the other Greek forms are copied as they appear and may contain printing errors.
